bib.title: CogAgent: A Visual Language Model for GUI Agents

read.skipped: References skimmed; figure images (Figs 1, 5-19) not viewable as text

question: Can a generalist vision-language model that reads only screenshots, at high resolution and within a manageable compute budget, beat HTML-reading LLMs on GUI navigation while staying strong on general VQA?
hypothesis: GUI screenshots need high resolution for tiny text and icons, and a small-hidden-size cross-attention branch can supply that cheaply; GUI-specific pre-training data further helps.
contributions: High-resolution cross-module added to CogVLM-17B, giving 1120x1120 input at lower compute
CCS400K web screenshot dataset with 140M REC and REG QA pairs plus OCR and grounding pre-training data
State of the art on nine VQA benchmarks as a generalist, and on Mind2Web and AITW using screenshots only

method.summary: CogAgent adds a 0.30B EVA2-CLIP-L high-resolution branch, fused by small-hidden-size cross-attention into every layer of the CogVLM-17B decoder. It is pre-trained 60k steps on OCR, grounding, GUI and caption data, then multi-task fine-tuned 10k steps on VQA, human-annotated screenshots and converted Mind2Web and AITW data.
method.task: GUI understanding and navigation (next-action prediction), plus VQA

evidence.quote: Training time is evaluated on A800 with the batch size of 8.

results.claim: CogAgent, from screenshots only, reaches 58.2 overall step SR on Mind2Web, above every HTML-input LLM compared.
results.setup: Mind2Web, three out-of-domain test subsets, step SR, candidates top-50 (GPT-4 row top-10), CogAgent fine-tuned on the Mind2Web train set from screenshots only

results.claim: Fine-tuned LLaMA2-70B on cleaned HTML scores 54.4 overall on Mind2Web.
results.setup: Mind2Web, authors fine-tuned LLaMA2-70B with the Deng et al. HTML cleansing, top-50 candidates

results.claim: Few-shot GPT-4 on HTML scores 30.9 overall on Mind2Web; the number is copied from Deng et al. and uses top-10 candidates, unlike the top-50 of the fine-tuned rows.
results.setup: Mind2Web, GPT-4 few-shot, HTML input, element selection from top-10 candidates (dagger), result from Deng et al.
results.note: Dagger marks top-10 candidate selection; other rows use top-50, so the comparison with 58.2 is not like for like.

results.claim: CogAgent beats LLaMA2-70B by 11.6, 4.7 and 6.6 points on cross-task, cross-website and cross-domain.
results.setup: Mind2Web, three out-of-domain test subsets, step SR, candidates top-50 (GPT-4 row top-10), CogAgent fine-tuned on the Mind2Web train set from screenshots only
results.quote: surpassing LLaMA2-70B, which is nearly 4× the scale of CogAgent, by 11.6%, 4.7%, and 6.6%, respectively

results.claim: On AITW CogAgent scores 76.88 overall, +2.61 over the visual baseline Auto-UI (74.27) and far above language baselines using OCR+icon text.
results.setup: AITW, unified model fine-tuned on all five subsets, GoogleApps subset downsampled to 10%
results.quote: our model achieves +2.61 improvements in the overall performance

results.claim: Language-model baselines on AITW overall: GPT-3.5 few-shot 7.72, LLaMA2-7B 28.40 (the latter fine-tuned per subset), both from Zhan and Zhang.
results.table: Table 4, rows GPT-3.5 and LLaMA2-7B, column Overall

results.claim: In a sampled manual re-check of mismatches with the AITW labels, 42% were valid alternative actions, not errors.
results.metric: share of sampled mismatches that were correct
results.setup: AITW, sample of CogAgent responses that differ from the label; sample size not given beyond 'hundreds'
results.note: Main text says 'randomly sample hundreds of cases ... more than 40% are determined to be correct'; appendix says 42% of 'sampled instances'. Sample size is never given as a number.
results.quote: in 42% of these, the model’s response actually represented an alternative correct method

results.claim: High-resolution cross-module cuts forward FLOPs: 12.56 TFLOPs at 224 plus 1120 versus 29.14 for the original architecture at 490.
results.setup: Ablation, CogVLM-style architecture vs cross-module, forward pass; batch size 8 for training time; Table 5

results.claim: At 1120 resolution the original architecture needs 143.2 TFLOPs, more than ten times the cross-module's 12.56 (value read from Fig 3 labels).
results.setup: Fig 3, forward propagation; the figure's labels are 7.8, 8.8, 10.1, 12.6, 29.1, 66.3, 143.2
results.note: 143.2 is read from figure labels in the text layer, not stated in prose.
results.quote: Its FLOPs can even be more than 10 times higher compared to employing a cross-module at a resolution of 1120

results.claim: The paper claims at least (6400+LT)/(256+LT) times lower attention complexity and over 25x in early pre-training.
results.setup: Attention-complexity derivation, LT below 512, d_cross=32, H_cross=32, d_dec=128, H_dec=32
results.note: Theory of attention cost only, not measured wall clock.
results.quote: our high-resolution cross-module can get an over 25× reduction in computational cost

results.claim: CogAgent reaches 52.8 on MM-Vet (zero-shot) and 85.9 on POPE-adversarial.
results.setup: Zero-shot, MM-Vet test; POPE adversarial subset F1 85.9
results.quote: our model achieved a remarkable score of 52.8, surpassing the closest competitor, LLaVA-1.5, by a substantial margin (+16.5)

results.claim: Generalist VQA results: TextVQA 76.1, DocVQA 81.6, ChartQA 68.4, InfoVQA 44.5, STVQA 80.5, VQAv2 83.7, OKVQA 61.2, OCRVQA 75.0.
results.setup: Single generalist model fine-tuned jointly on all eight VQA sets

results.claim: Ablation: adding OCR then GUI and grounding pre-train data lifts Mind2Web from 38.6 (Cap) to 54.2 (All) and DocVQA from 57.6 to 76.4.
results.setup: Ablation: shorter fine-tune (2,400 iters, batch 128) on Mind2Web, top-10; 'All' uses base 224 and cross 1120

results.claim: In the architecture ablation, cross-module at 756 gives STVQA 73.6 vs 68.1 for the original at 490 while using about half the TFLOPs (10.08 vs 29.14).
results.setup: Ablation, models pre-trained with Caption+OCR data; training time/it on A800 batch 8

results.claim: The cross-module branch adds 0.30B parameters; pre-training first trains only 646M (3.5%) of the parameters.
results.quote: resulting in a total number of 646M (3.5%) trainable parameters

limits: Authors concede imprecise output coordinates and inability to process multiple images (Conclusion).
AITW action matching undercounts valid alternative paths; authors recommend a virtual-environment task-completion evaluation.
Mind2Web comparison mixes top-10 (GPT-4) and top-50 candidates, and mixes few-shot with fine-tuned baselines.
Mind2Web and AITW are offline next-action benchmarks, not live task completion.
Single runs, no seeds or variance; step counts for task fine-tuning and decoding settings not given.
Failure cases: incorrect action, incorrect coordinate, incorrect GUI observation, hallucination (Appendix 7).
The 18B version is dated; the authors point to CogAgent-9B-20241220.
